name: Proxmox_VE_Disks
description: Physical disk SMART health, size and SSD life remaining for every disk on every online node.
technicalNotes:
BatchScript, one /nodes/{node}/disks/list call per online node per interval. Requires Sys.Audit on / or on /nodes/{node}. O(nodes).

This endpoint shells out to smartctl for every disk on the node, so it runs on a deliberately long interval. Partitions are not requested: a partition's SMART health is the health of the disk beneath it, and including them would duplicate every instance.

Two fields are not what they appear, and both are handled deliberately:

health is a string that defaults to "UNKNOWN" when smartctl could not be read -- that is an absence of verdict, not a failure. It is therefore reported as two datapoints: SmartHealthKnown says whether there is a verdict at all, and SmartHealthOK says what it was -- and SmartHealthOK is withheld entirely when there is no verdict. Emitting a zero there would make an unreadable disk alert exactly like a failing one, which is the mistake this split exists to prevent.

wearout is the literal string "N/A" on anything that is not SSD-like and wherever the wear attribute is missing, so LifeRemainingPercent is emitted only when the value is genuinely numeric. A zero there would read as a disk with no life left. LifeRemainingKnown carries that distinction as a datapoint of its own, so a spinning disk reads as an explicit 0 rather than as a gap.

LifeRemainingPercent is Proxmox's wearout value, which its Diskmanage source computes as 100 minus the NVMe percentage-used, and as the normalised SMART wear attribute for SATA SSDs -- both of which are life *remaining*, so the threshold alerts when it falls. Confirmed against real SSD and NVMe disks on 2026-09-22: the direction is right and the threshold is the correct way round.

datapoints.name: SizeGB
datapoints.description: Disk capacity in GB (decimal, 10^9 bytes), the same figure as SizeBytes in a unit a dashboard table can print. LogicMonitor renders a raw byte count of this magnitude in scientific notation.

datapoints.name: SmartHealthOK
datapoints.description: 1 when SMART reports the disk as PASSED or OK, 0 when it reports a failure. Emitted only when a verdict exists: a disk whose SMART cannot be read reports no data here rather than a zero, so it cannot alert as though it were failing. Check SmartHealthKnown to tell the two situations apart.
datapoints.alertBody: SMART reports disk ##INSTANCE## as failing. This datapoint is only reported when smartctl returned a real verdict, so this is a genuine failure verdict rather than an unreadable disk.

datapoints.name: SmartHealthKnown
datapoints.description: 1 when smartctl returned a real verdict. 0 means UNKNOWN or SMART disabled, so SmartHealthOK carries no information.

datapoints.name: Mounted
datapoints.description: 1 when the disk is mounted on the node.

datapoints.name: LifeRemainingKnown
datapoints.description: 1 when the disk reports a wear attribute, which in practice means an SSD or NVMe. 0 on a spinning disk, where LifeRemainingPercent is deliberately absent rather than zero.

datapoints.name: LifeRemainingPercent
datapoints.description: SSD life remaining, percent, from Proxmox's wearout value. Reported only for disks that expose a wear attribute; absent elsewhere rather than zero. Check LifeRemainingKnown to tell a spinning disk apart from a collection failure.
